Recovery, discussed their services.

Springs Neighborhood.

Limor Magen, Westlake Village, commented on drones flying at Canyon Oaks Park.

l  Michael Berkovitz, Thousand Oaks, encouraged residents to attend the Relay for Life
  event on October 1, 2022, 9:00 am -9:00 pm, at California Lutheran University Memorial
  Stadium.

  Cristy Warner and students, Thousand Oaks, encouraged residents to attend the Relay
  for Life event on October 1, 2022, 9:00 am - 9:00 pm, California Lutheran University
  Memorial Stadium.

  COUNCIL RESPONSE:

  Councilmember Mcsweeney and Mayor Pro Tern Pearl expressed appreciation to Ms.
  Magen for conveying her drone concerns.

  STAFF COMMENTS:

  City Manager de Geus highlighted the summer concert series and 4th of July Parade and
  Fireworks. Mr. de Geus stated the recycled water line is now active at Canyon Oaks
  Park; all parks now use recycled water for irrigation. The planter refurbishment project at
  Berniece Bennett Park was completed, the City-wide Landscape Maintenance Request
  for Proposal was issued and staff reviewed and presented responses to the
  Environmental Committee for consideration. He added that recruitments for Accountant
  11 and Public Services Inspector positions closed in August, the first phase of the annual
  audit was completed, and minor interior improvements were completed at City Hall.

  On August 31, Los Angeles County Fire Department, along with staff and Community
  Emergency Response Team volunteers, distributed National Oceanic and Atmospheric
  Administration radios along with emergency preparedness information to over 200
  residents. The radios will function when there is no power to hear information distributed
  by the weather service.

  Lastly, City Manager de Geus reported that there were a few burglaries this summer, both
  residential and commercial. Mr. de Geus stated that while we have a very safe community
  with a low crime rate, any occurrence is concerning. The City has invested in additional

j  Sheriff patrols in response to the burglaries and is developing improvements to enhance
  the City's prevention and responses to crime. On September 28, Captain Seetoo, Lost
  Hills Sheriff's Station, will discuss these burglary concerns, along with prevention and
  response tools. Mr. de Geus reminded the community to remain vigilant about crime and
  report any concerns to the Sheriff.

  COUNCIL COMMENTS:

  Councilmember Davis reported attending the League of Cal Cities Conference,
  September 7-9, 2022, Long Beach, along with Mayor Halpern and city staff and
  commented on the educational topics.

City of Westlake Village  September 14, 2022  4

COUNCIL COMMENTS (continued):

Mayor Pro Tern Pearl appreciated the public safety comments and recommended a study
session to go more in-depth on public safety and to discuss additional tools/options
available for consideration.

Councilmember Mcsweeney concurred with the Public Safety study session noting
residents would like this topic addressed.

Mayor Halpern agreed with the recommendation to hold a Public Safety study session
and reminded residents to contact the Sheriff with any concerns. Mr. Halpern cautioned
residents to keep pets safe from coyote endangerment.

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

1.  Administrative Committee Report

  City Manager de Geus introduced the Community Survey stating that in 2019 City
  Council approved a Community Survey with True North Research. Historically,
  since 2009, the survey was conducted approximately every five years. With the
  onset of COVlD-19, the survey was postponed, and staff resumed work on the
  survey in 2022. On May 31, 2022, the Administrative Committee (Mayor Halpern
  and Mayor Pro Tern Pearl) reviewed the survey and recommended that staff
  reinstate the community survey. Mr. de Geus stated that the community survey
  budget has been added to the continued budget appropriations agenda item this
  evening for City Council approval.

  Timothy Mclarney, President of True North Research, presented an overview of
  the Community Survey, including a timeline and survey topics.

  City Council inquired whether COVID-19 will affect survey results and the
  possibility of additional survey questions or modifying existing survey questions to
  include perceptions related to law enforcement/crime, drought and schools in the
  survey. The City Manager stated that the survey is already very long, but he will
  work the Timothy Mclarney to explore how to incorporate these topics further into
  the survey.

  No formal action taken by City Council on this agenda item .

  2. ZERO EMISSIONS LEAF BLOWER ORDINANCE; ORDINANCE NO. 296-22

  Planning Director Forbes introduced the Zero Emissions Leaf Blower Ordinance
  highlighting that City Council requested staff to proceed with parallel efforts to
  transition city maintenance contracts to zero emissions and to prohibit gasoline
  powered equipment in 2023.

  Planning Director Forbes stated the proposed ordinance will prohibit all leaf
  blowers powered by gasoline or combustion engines as of January 1, 2023, thus
  reducing air pollution, noise pollution, and the health effects of using gasoline
  blowers. Planning Director Forbes noted public outreach and education will ensure
  residents and those working in the City are aware of the Zero Emission ordinance,
  noting that future outreach will include a bilingual flyer/postcard that homeowners
  and Homeowner Associations can share with gardeners. Lastly, grant and
  equipment exchange programs will be shared as the State releases these
  opportunities.

  The second ordinance prohibiting additional gas-powered landscape equipment
  will be presented later this year to City Council for approval.

  Councilmember Davis moved to introduce Ordinance No. 296-22, titled 'An
  Ordinance of the City of Westlake Village Regarding Leaf Blowers and Amending
  the Westlake Village Municipal Code' by title only and that further reading be
  waived. Councilmember Honig seconded the motion.

  Pearl, and Mayor Halpern

1.  PURE WATER PROJECT UPDATE - LAS VIRGENES TRIUNFO JOINT
  POWERS AUTHORITY

  Planning Director Forbes introduced the Pure Water project proposed by the Las
  Virgenes-Triunfo Joint Powers Authority (JPA), a partnership between the Las
  Virgenes Municipal Water District (LVMWD) and the Triunfo Water and Sanitation
  District.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  September 14, 2022  9

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  LVMWD Board Director, Leonard Polan, provided an overview of the JPA and the
  operation of the Tapia Water Reclamation Facility, treating wastewater to produce
  recycled water. Mr. Polan explained that due to changes in water regulations,
  surplus recycled water will no longer be able to be discharged into Malibu Creek
  unless it is cleaned to a point that exceeds drinking water standards. Rather than
  discharging this water, the JPA is proposing to treat and reuse the water through
  the Pure Water potable reuse project.

  Oliver Slosser, LVMWD Engineering Program Manager, reviewed how the Pure
  Water project will take surplus recycled water from the Tapia facility and deliver it
  to a new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) for further treatment. Mr.
  Slosser said the facility will use advanced technologies to purify the recycled water
  to meet or exceed State drinking water standards. The purified water will then be
  piped to the Las Virgenes Reservoir in Westlake Village where it will be blended
  with the existing reservoir water and become part of the potable water supply.

  The Pure Water project is anticipated to begin construction in late 2025, complete
  construction by the end of 2027, and be fully operational by 2030. Mr. Slosser
  discussed the two possible site locations for the new AWPF that are under review
  in the Draft Environmental Impact Report, which allows for public comments until
  October 7, 2022 (online at www.ourpureh2o.com).

  City Council discussed the two proposed AWPF site locations and expressed
  supporting a site that has the least environmental impact, inquired on the
  chemicals and processes used in the purification process, and thanked LVMWD
  for the project that will result in a new local water source.

  City staff will provide a status update on the drafting of the City of Westlake Village
  comment letter regarding the Draft Environmental Impact Report at the City
  Council meeting on September 28, 2022.
